ace-cpt-readiness-check-client-interview.prompt: Sofia, 33, has a measured resting heart rate of 65 bpm and an estimated HRmax of 185 bpm. Her trainer sets steady-state cardio at 60–70% of heart-rate reserve. Which target zone should he program?
ace-cpt-readiness-check-client-interview.explanation: Karvonen: target HR = (HRmax − resting HR) × intensity + resting HR. Heart-rate reserve = 185 − 65 = 120 bpm. 0.60 × 120 + 65 = 137 bpm and 0.70 × 120 + 65 = 149 bpm, so the zone is 137–149 bpm.

distractorExplanations.a: Takes 60–70% of the heart-rate reserve but forgets to add back the 65-bpm resting heart rate, giving a zone barely above rest.
distractorExplanations.b: Applies 60–70% to HRmax (185) instead of to heart-rate reserve; percent-of-max zones run lower than the same HRR percentages.
distractorExplanations.d: Mixes the two methods by adding resting HR to a percent of HRmax; the top of that zone exceeds her 185-bpm maximum.

ace-cpt-readiness-check-instruction-010.prompt: Client Malik is pressing 32-kg dumbbells on a flat bench, aiming for a 6-rep max set. Trainer Erin will spot him. Where should Erin position her hands during the set?

options.a: Under his elbows, ready to push his upper arms up
options.b: At his wrists, as close to the dumbbells as possible
options.c: Off to the side, letting him drop the bells on failure
options.d: Under the dumbbells, helping lift them on every rep

ace-cpt-readiness-check-instruction-010.explanation: For dumbbell presses, the spotter's hands go at the wrists, close to the weights, because that is where the load can be controlled. Spotting at the elbows lets the forearms tip and the dumbbells fall toward the face or chest. Agree on cues and a racking plan before the set.

distractorExplanations.a: Elbow support cannot control the dumbbells; the forearms can collapse inward or outward and drop the weights onto the face or chest.
distractorExplanations.c: Dropping 32-kg dumbbells from a failed press risks hitting the face, chest, or shoulders; a near-max set needs a hands-ready spotter.
distractorExplanations.d: Lifting the bells on every rep turns the set into assisted reps and removes the overload; the spotter helps when the lifter stalls.

ace-cpt-readiness-check-professional-009.prompt: Midway through a session, client Rachel reports right-knee pain of 6/10 during squats. She slipped on ice two days ago, and the knee looks swollen. What should trainer Ben do?

options.a: Drop the load and finish the squats, since pain is below 7/10
options.b: Massage and stretch her quad to release the tension at the knee
options.c: Suggest 400 mg of ibuprofen and move her to the leg press
options.d: Stop knee loading, log the incident, and refer her to a doctor

ace-cpt-readiness-check-professional-009.explanation: New swelling and 6/10 pain after a fall are red flags for an acute injury that a licensed clinician must evaluate. Trainers stop the aggravating activity, document the incident, and refer; diagnosing, manual therapy, and medication advice fall outside a personal trainer's scope.

distractorExplanations.a: There is no safe pain cutoff for training through a new, swollen injury; pain after trauma means stopping, not lowering the load.
distractorExplanations.b: Hands-on soft-tissue treatment of an injured joint is manual therapy, which is outside a trainer's scope and may worsen the injury.
distractorExplanations.c: Recommending medication doses is outside trainer scope, and a leg press still loads the swollen knee before any medical evaluation.

acsm-cpt-readiness-check-assessment-009.prompt: Carla, 52, has not exercised regularly in years, was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes last year, and reports no signs or symptoms. Under ACSM preparticipation screening, what is the appropriate next step?

options.a: Start moderate exercise now; clearance is for vigorous work
options.b: Count her risk factors; with two or more she needs a stress test
options.c: Get medical clearance, then begin light-to-moderate exercise
options.d: Skip clearance, as she has no signs or symptoms of disease

acsm-cpt-readiness-check-assessment-009.explanation: ACSM screening checks current exercise habits, then known cardiovascular, metabolic, or renal disease, then signs or symptoms. An inactive client with known type 2 diabetes, even without symptoms, needs medical clearance; after clearance she starts light-to-moderate exercise and progresses gradually.

distractorExplanations.a: That rule fits clients who already exercise regularly; inactive clients with known metabolic disease need clearance before starting.
distractorExplanations.b: Risk-factor counting was dropped from ACSM's screening algorithm in 2015, and routine exercise testing is not required before starting.
distractorExplanations.d: Lack of symptoms does not cancel known disease; for an inactive client, diagnosed diabetes alone triggers medical clearance.

acsm-cpt-readiness-check-programming-004.prompt: Omar weighs 80 kg and is prescribed 40 minutes of stationary cycling at 5 METs, four days a week, for weight loss. Using ACSM's metabolic formula, how many kilocalories does one session burn?

options.a: About 7 kcal
options.b: About 280 kcal
options.c: About 400 kcal
options.d: About 1,400 kcal

acsm-cpt-readiness-check-programming-004.explanation: ACSM: kcal/min = METs × 3.5 × body mass (kg) ÷ 200. Here 5 × 3.5 × 80 ÷ 200 = 7 kcal/min, and 7 × 40 min = 280 kcal per session. Dividing by 200 converts mL of oxygen to kcal (about 5 kcal per liter of O2).

distractorExplanations.a: Stops at the per-minute rate; 7 kcal/min must be multiplied by the 40-minute session to get the total energy cost.
distractorExplanations.c: Treats 1 MET as 1 kcal/kg for the whole session (5 × 80); that shortcut is per hour, so 40 minutes gives about 267 kcal, not 400.
distractorExplanations.d: Reports oxygen use (5 × 3.5 × 80 = 1,400 mL O2/min) as kcal; dividing by 200 converts it to 7 kcal per minute.

acsm-cpt-readiness-check-science-007.prompt: After hard cycling intervals, Paul, 45, stops pedaling abruptly and steps off the bike. Within a minute he is lightheaded and pale. He has no diabetes and ate two hours ago. What is the most likely cause and response?

options.a: Low blood sugar; give him juice and restart the intervals
options.b: Lactic acid buildup; stretch his legs to flush it out faster
options.c: Dehydration; have him drink water and finish his session
options.d: Blood pooling in the legs; lie him down with legs raised

acsm-cpt-readiness-check-science-007.explanation: Stopping abruptly removes the skeletal-muscle pump, so blood pools in the dilated leg vessels, venous return and blood pressure drop, and the brain is briefly underperfused. Lying down with legs raised restores venous return; an active cool-down prevents a repeat.

distractorExplanations.a: Sudden onset right after stopping, in a man without diabetes who ate recently, fits venous pooling; restarting intervals adds risk.
distractorExplanations.b: Lactate does not cause fainting and is cleared by light activity, not stretching; the trigger here is the sudden loss of the muscle pump.
distractorExplanations.c: Fluids help over time but do not explain onset within a minute of stopping, and finishing the session while lightheaded risks a fall.

ak-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.prompt: At one Juneau brokerage, the broker designates agent Cole for seller Pam and agent Dee for buyer Max on the same home, with both clients' written consent. Over coffee, Cole tells Dee that Pam must sell fast because of a job transfer. What is true?

options.a: Cole breached his duty by sharing Pam's confidential motive
options.b: No breach, since one brokerage owes both clients equal duties
options.c: Dee must keep the remark from Max, acting as Pam's subagent
options.d: Designated agency makes Cole and Dee dual agents who share facts

ak-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: In designated agency the broker appoints separate agents inside one firm, each representing just their own client. Cole owes Pam confidentiality, so revealing her need for a quick sale to the buyer's designated agent is a breach. The internal split exists precisely so each client's confidential information stays with that client's agent.

distractorExplanations.b: Designation gives each client an agent loyal to them; sharing inside the firm does not make Pam's motive fair game.
distractorExplanations.c: Dee is Max's designated agent, not Pam's subagent; her loyalty runs to Max, which is why Cole's disclosure harmed Pam.
distractorExplanations.d: Designated agents are not dual agents swapping information; each represents one side, and confidential facts stay on that side.

ak-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.prompt: Contractor Sam finished a $28,000 addition on Jill's Fairbanks home, but Jill never paid him. Sam timely records a mechanic's lien. A month later Jill signs a contract to sell the home. How does the lien affect the sale?

options.a: No effect, because it is a personal claim against Jill herself
options.b: It becomes a general lien on every parcel Jill owns
options.c: It must be paid or released for the buyer to get clear title
options.d: It is extinguished once the deed to the buyer is recorded

ak-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: A mechanic's lien is a specific, involuntary lien on the improved property itself, securing payment for labor and materials. It stays attached to the home through a sale, so the title company will require it to be paid off or released, often from Jill's proceeds at closing, before the buyer receives clear title.

distractorExplanations.a: The lien is recorded against the real estate, not just Jill personally, so it follows the property and clouds the title.
distractorExplanations.b: Mechanic's liens are specific liens limited to the improved property; judgment liens are the general kind that reach all real estate.
distractorExplanations.d: Recording a deed does not erase a recorded lien. A buyer takes title subject to it unless it is paid or released.

ak-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.prompt: Seller Nora closes on April 30, 2027. The year's $4,380 property taxes are paid in arrears and still unpaid. Using a 365-day year, with the seller responsible through closing day, how does the tax proration appear on the closing statement?

options.a: Credit Nora and debit the buyer $1,440 each
options.b: Debit Nora and credit the buyer $2,940 each
options.c: Credit Nora $2,940 and debit the buyer $2,940
options.d: Debit Nora and credit the buyer $1,440 each

ak-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: Daily tax: $4,380 ÷ 365 = $12. Nora owns January 1 through April 30, which is 120 days (31 + 28 + 31 + 30), so her share is 120 × $12 = $1,440. The taxes are unpaid and the buyer will pay the full bill later, so the seller is debited and the buyer credited $1,440.

distractorExplanations.a: Reverses the entries. The seller is credited when she prepaid the taxes; unpaid taxes mean she owes the buyer her share.
distractorExplanations.b: Right direction, wrong days: $2,940 is the buyer's 245 days (May 1 to December 31), not Nora's 120 days.
distractorExplanations.c: Uses the buyer's 245 days and the prepaid-tax direction; Nora neither paid ahead nor owns May through December.

al-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.prompt: Listing agent Beth, whose Mobile listing agreement does not authorize her to sign contracts, accepts a buyer's offer for traveling seller Jim. On his return, Jim reviews the terms and signs a written approval of the deal. How did Beth gain authority?

options.a: By ratification, through Jim's approval after the fact
options.b: By ostensible agency, since the buyer trusted Beth's title
options.c: By express agency created when Beth signed the acceptance
options.d: By the listing agreement, which lets agents bind sellers

al-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Ratification creates agency after the fact: when a principal knowingly approves an act done without authority, the act binds him as if it had been authorized from the start. Jim reviewed and approved Beth's unauthorized acceptance in writing. Ostensible agency instead rests on the principal's earlier conduct leading a third party to believe authority existed.

distractorExplanations.b: Ostensible agency comes from the principal's own conduct creating apparent authority before the act; here Jim's later approval bound him.
distractorExplanations.c: Express agency is granted by the principal in advance. Beth's own act of signing cannot give her authority she lacked.
distractorExplanations.d: A typical listing hires the broker to find a buyer; it does not authorize signing contracts that bind the seller.

al-real-estate-readiness-check-al-licens.prompt: An Alabama licensee helps a first-time buyer tour homes and write an offer, but they never sign a written agency agreement. The buyer later claims the licensee owed her loyalty as her agent. Under RECAD, what was the relationship?

options.a: Single agent for the buyer, created by helping write the offer
options.b: Transaction broker, as no written agency agreement exists
options.c: Subagent of the listing broker, the default under state law
options.d: Dual agent for both the buyer and the seller in the deal

al-real-estate-readiness-check-al-licens.explanation: Under Alabama's Real Estate Consumer's Agency and Disclosure Act (RECAD), a licensee is treated as a transaction broker, assisting without representing either party, unless a written agreement establishes an agency relationship. Touring homes and writing an offer did not create buyer agency here.

distractorExplanations.a: Helping with tours and an offer does not create single agency under RECAD; that relationship requires a written agreement.
distractorExplanations.c: Subagency is not the RECAD default; the default is transaction broker, which represents neither side.
distractorExplanations.d: Dual agency requires informed written consent from both parties; with no written agreement at all, the licensee is a transaction broker.

al-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.prompt: Seller Ruth's purchase contract lists no exclusions. Before closing she removes a custom wall bookcase bolted into a niche built for it, saying she always meant to take it. The buyer objects. Who most likely is entitled to the bookcase?

options.a: Ruth, because her intention to remove it controls
options.b: Ruth, since bookcases are furniture and stay personal property
options.c: Ruth, because removing it before closing ends the buyer's claim
options.d: The buyer, since attachment and custom fit make it a fixture

al-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Courts apply the fixture tests: method of attachment, adaptation to the property, relationship of the parties, intent shown objectively, and the parties' agreement. The bookcase is bolted in and built for that niche, and the contract excludes nothing, so it conveys with the real estate. A seller's unstated intent does not override those facts.

distractorExplanations.a: Intent is judged by objective facts such as attachment and adaptation, not by a private plan Ruth never put in the contract.
distractorExplanations.b: Freestanding furniture is personal property, but a bookcase bolted into a custom niche has become part of the real estate.
distractorExplanations.c: Removing a fixture before closing does not defeat the buyer's right; the buyer may demand it back or seek its value.

ar-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.prompt: Listing agent Tom represents Fayetteville seller Erin, who privately told him she would take $30,000 under list. An unrepresented buyer asks Tom whether Erin will go lower and whether the roof has leaked; Tom knows it leaked last spring. What should Tom do?

options.a: Disclose the roof leak but keep Erin's price flexibility private
options.b: Disclose both facts, since the buyer asked direct questions
options.c: Keep both private, since his duty of loyalty runs to Erin
options.d: Tell the buyer Erin will accept less but stay silent on the roof leak

ar-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: A seller's agent owes the seller confidentiality, so Erin's willingness to take less stays private. But every licensee owes all parties honesty and must disclose known material defects, so Tom must reveal the roof leak. Loyalty to the client does not permit concealing a material fact from a buyer-customer.

distractorExplanations.b: A direct question does not override confidentiality; revealing Erin's lowest acceptable price would breach his duty to his client.
distractorExplanations.c: Loyalty covers Erin's negotiating position, not known defects. Hiding the leak would be misrepresentation to the buyer.
distractorExplanations.d: This reverses the duties: price flexibility is confidential, while the known roof leak is a material fact he must disclose.

ar-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.prompt: Buyer Wes is about to close on a Fort Smith lot when the title search shows a recorded lis pendens: the seller's former business partner has sued, claiming a half interest in the lot. What does the notice mean for Wes?

options.a: No effect, since a lis pendens is notice and not a lien
options.b: The partner has already won half ownership by a court judgment
options.c: If he closes now, he takes title subject to the suit's result
options.d: The law prohibits any transfer of the lot until the case ends

ar-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: A lis pendens is recorded notice that a lawsuit affecting title or possession is pending. It gives constructive notice, so anyone who buys now is bound by the court's eventual ruling. It does not decide ownership or legally block the sale, but most buyers and title insurers will not close until it is resolved.

distractorExplanations.a: It is not a lien, but it still binds later buyers: anyone acquiring the lot takes subject to whatever the court decides.
distractorExplanations.b: A lis pendens shows a case is pending, not decided. A judgment would come later and might reject the partner's claim.
distractorExplanations.d: The notice warns buyers rather than forbidding a sale; the risk is taking title subject to the suit, not a legal ban.

ar-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.prompt: Buyer Ana's lender hands her the Closing Disclosure in person on a Thursday, and no federal holiday falls in the following week. Under TRID's three-business-day rule, what is the earliest day her loan can be consummated?

options.a: Saturday, counting Thursday as the first day
options.b: Tuesday, since Saturday is not a business day
options.c: The next Thursday, after a 7-business-day wait
options.d: Monday, counting Saturday as a business day

ar-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: The Closing Disclosure must be received at least three business days before consummation, and for this rule a business day is every day except Sundays and federal holidays. From Thursday receipt: Friday (1), Saturday (2), Monday (3), so consummation may occur Monday. The 7-business-day lead time applies to the Loan Estimate, not the CD.

distractorExplanations.a: The day of receipt does not count; the three days start the next day, so Thursday cannot be day one.
distractorExplanations.b: For the Closing Disclosure timing rule, Saturdays are business days; just Sundays and federal holidays are skipped.
distractorExplanations.c: Seven business days is the Loan Estimate lead time before consummation; the Closing Disclosure needs three.

az-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.prompt: Tucson seller Helen signs a six-month exclusive listing with broker Ray. Two months later, before any offer is accepted, Helen dies. Her daughter, the named executor, calls Ray to ask where things stand. What is the status of the listing?

options.a: It continues, and the executor must honor its terms
options.b: It continues until the six-month term expires
options.c: It ended at Helen's death; the estate may relist
options.d: It ends once Ray signs a written release for the estate

az-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: A listing creates a personal agency relationship, and the death of either the principal or the broker terminates it automatically by operation of law. Ray has no authority to keep marketing the home. Once the executor has authority to act for the estate, she can sign a new listing if the heirs want to sell.

distractorExplanations.a: Confuses a sale contract with agency; an accepted purchase contract may bind the estate, but agency authority ends at the principal's death.
distractorExplanations.b: The term sets the maximum length of the listing; the principal's death ends the agency earlier by operation of law.
distractorExplanations.d: No release is needed; termination by death is automatic and requires no action by the broker or the estate.

az-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.prompt: Walter deeds his Scottsdale condo to his nephew Ben 'for the life of Walter's sister, Rose,' naming no remainderman. Ben lives there for years, then dies while Rose is still alive. Who holds the right to possess the condo now?

options.a: Walter, because the estate reverts when Ben dies
options.b: Rose, because the estate is measured by her life
options.c: Ben's estate, which now owns it in fee simple
options.d: Ben's heirs or devisees, until Rose dies

az-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: This is a life estate pur autre vie: Ben's estate lasts for Rose's life, not his own. Because the measuring life is still alive, Ben's interest passes to his heirs or devisees, who hold it until Rose dies. At Rose's death the property reverts to Walter or his estate, since no remainderman was named.

distractorExplanations.a: Treats it as an ordinary life estate measured by Ben's own life; Walter's reversion waits for Rose's death.
distractorExplanations.b: Rose is the measuring life, not an owner; being named in the deed gives her no right to possess the condo.
distractorExplanations.c: A life estate does not grow into fee simple; Ben's heirs hold it until the measuring life ends, then it reverts.

az-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-a.prompt: A Mesa fourplex grosses $72,000 a year. Vacancy and credit loss run 5%, operating expenses are $20,400, and the owner's mortgage payments total $12,000 a year. At a 6% market cap rate, what value does the income approach indicate?
az-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-a.explanation: Value = NOI ÷ cap rate. Effective gross income is $72,000 − 5% vacancy = $68,400. Subtracting $20,400 of operating expenses leaves NOI of $48,000. Debt service is a financing cost, not an operating expense, so it is ignored. $48,000 ÷ 0.06 = $800,000.

distractorExplanations.a: Subtracts the $12,000 mortgage payments; debt service depends on the owner's financing and is excluded from NOI.
distractorExplanations.c: Skips the 5% vacancy and credit loss, capitalizing $51,600 instead of the true $48,000 NOI.
distractorExplanations.d: Capitalizes gross income; the income approach divides net operating income, after vacancy and expenses, by the cap rate.

cfp-certification-readiness-check-planni.prompt: A Monte Carlo analysis for the Garcias, retiring at 62 and spending $90,000 a year, shows a 58% probability of success. They want more confidence. What is the planner's most appropriate next step?

options.a: Model changes like later retirement or lower spending, then rerun
options.b: Raise the assumed rate of return until the success rate reaches 90%
options.c: Explain that they should expect 58% of their target retirement income
options.d: Move the portfolio to 100% equities to lift expected returns

cfp-certification-readiness-check-planni.explanation: A 58% result means 42% of simulated return paths ran out of money. The planner should test realistic levers the clients control, such as retiring later, spending less, or saving more, and rerun the simulation rather than changing assumptions to manufacture a better number.

distractorExplanations.b: Inflating the return assumption manufactures a higher success rate without changing the real risk; assumptions must stay reasonable.
distractorExplanations.c: Misreads the output: 58% is the share of simulated trials that fund the full goal, not the share of income they will receive.
distractorExplanations.d: Ignores their risk tolerance; more equity volatility can worsen sequence risk early in retirement and need not raise success.

cfp-certification-readiness-check-invest.prompt: A client's entire portfolio will be one fund. Fund X returned 12% with a 20% standard deviation and beta 1.2; Fund Y returned 9% with a 10% standard deviation and beta 0.9. T-bills yield 3%. Which conclusion is correct?

options.a: Fund X, with the higher Treynor ratio of 7.50 versus 6.67
options.b: Fund Y, with the higher Sharpe ratio of 0.60 versus 0.45
options.c: Fund X, because its 12% total return is the highest
options.d: Fund Y, because its lower beta means lower total risk

cfp-certification-readiness-check-invest.explanation: When one fund is the whole portfolio, total risk matters, so use the Sharpe ratio: (return − risk-free rate) ÷ standard deviation. Fund X: (12 − 3) ÷ 20 = 0.45. Fund Y: (9 − 3) ÷ 10 = 0.60. Fund Y earns more excess return per unit of total risk.

distractorExplanations.a: Treynor divides by beta and suits well-diversified portfolios; for a single-fund portfolio, unsystematic risk matters and Sharpe applies.
distractorExplanations.c: Raw return ignores risk; Fund X took twice the volatility to earn three extra points of return.
distractorExplanations.d: Beta captures market (systematic) risk, not total risk; the right reason to pick Fund Y is its higher Sharpe ratio.

cfp-certification-readiness-check-retire.prompt: Mia, 40, inherits a traditional IRA from her father, who died in 2025 at age 80, after his required beginning date. She is not disabled, chronically ill, or a minor child. How must she take distributions?

options.a: Over her own life expectancy, as a stretch IRA
options.b: Within 5 years of his death, with no annual RMDs
options.c: Annual RMDs in years 1-9, with a full payout by year 10
options.d: Any amounts she likes, provided it is empty by the end of year 10

cfp-certification-readiness-check-retire.explanation: Under the SECURE Act and the 2024 final regulations, a non-eligible designated beneficiary must empty the IRA by the end of the 10th year after death. Because her father died after his required beginning date, she must also take annual RMDs in years 1 through 9, starting in 2026.

distractorExplanations.a: Lifetime stretch is limited to eligible designated beneficiaries such as a spouse, minor child, or disabled heir; an adult child does not qualify.
distractorExplanations.b: The 5-year rule applies to non-designated beneficiaries, such as an estate, when the owner died before the required beginning date.
distractorExplanations.d: That flexible 10-year payout works when the owner dies before the required beginning date; dying after it adds annual RMDs.

co-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.prompt: Tenant Priya's lease on a Boulder duplex gives her a right of first refusal. The owner, Glen, receives a $640,000 offer from an investor and accepts it, subject to Priya's right. What may Priya do?

options.a: Force Glen to sell to her at a price fixed in her lease
options.b: Purchase on the same terms the investor offered
options.c: Cancel her lease without penalty because of the sale
options.d: Block the sale to the investor for the rest of her lease term

co-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: A right of first refusal lets the holder buy if and when the owner decides to sell, by matching a bona fide third-party offer. Glen chose to sell at $640,000, so Priya may buy on those terms or let the investor's deal go ahead. An option, by contrast, lets the holder buy at a preset price whenever she elects during the option period.

distractorExplanations.a: That describes an option contract, which fixes a price in advance. A right of first refusal ties her price to the outside offer.
distractorExplanations.c: A sale does not end an existing lease; the buyer takes title subject to Priya's tenancy, and the right gives her no penalty-free exit.
distractorExplanations.d: The right lets her match, not veto. If she declines to match, Glen may complete the sale to the investor.

co-real-estate-readiness-check-co-licens.prompt: Ana is moving to Denver to start a real estate career. Based on what she read about other states, she plans to get a salesperson license first and upgrade later. What should she know about Colorado licensing?

options.a: She must hold a salesperson license before she can apply as a broker
options.b: She needs a transaction-broker license to work with buyers and sellers
options.c: Colorado issues broker licenses and has no salesperson tier
options.d: She may practice under her employing broker's license for a year

co-real-estate-readiness-check-co-licens.explanation: The Colorado Real Estate Commission licenses brokers and has no separate salesperson license, so Ana applies for a broker license and works under an employing broker. Transaction-broker is a type of brokerage relationship with a consumer, not a license category anyone applies for.

distractorExplanations.a: Confuses Colorado with states that use a two-tier salesperson and broker system. Colorado has a single broker license.
distractorExplanations.b: Transaction-broker describes the working relationship with a consumer; it is not a license class issued by the Commission.
distractorExplanations.d: Anyone performing brokerage for others for a fee needs a license in her own name; working under another's license is unlicensed activity.

co-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.prompt: Jonah buys into a Denver cooperative: he receives shares in the corporation that owns the building and a proprietary lease. Several neighbors stop paying monthly charges that fund the building's single blanket mortgage. How does this affect Jonah?

options.a: No effect, since each owner has a separate mortgage on the unit
options.b: His deed to the unit shields him from the corporation's debts
options.c: The lender may foreclose the defaulting neighbors' units alone
options.d: He and the other shareholders may have to cover the shortfall

co-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: In a cooperative the corporation owns the building and carries one blanket mortgage; shareholders hold personal property (shares) plus a proprietary lease, not a deed. If some shareholders stop paying, the rest must make up the shortfall or the whole building can be foreclosed. Separate unit mortgages and deeds are features of a condominium.

distractorExplanations.a: Separate unit mortgages and tax bills describe a condominium. A co-op building is financed with one blanket mortgage owed by the corporation.
distractorExplanations.b: Co-op owners receive shares and a proprietary lease, not a deed; the corporation holds title to the whole building.
distractorExplanations.c: The units are not separately mortgaged. The blanket loan covers the entire building, so a foreclosure would reach every shareholder.

ct-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.prompt: At a Connecticut networking breakfast, broker Dana tells brokers from two competing firms that 'everyone in town should hold the line at 6% so sellers stop negotiating us down.' The others nod and agree. What is the main legal problem?

options.a: Competing brokers agreeing on a rate is price-fixing under antitrust law
options.b: It is fine as long as the 6% rate is disclosed in each listing contract
options.c: It is legal because commission rates are set by the state commission
options.d: It is acceptable because each broker can still lower the fee for a client who asks

ct-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Commission rates are negotiable between each broker and its client. When competitors agree to charge a set rate, that is price-fixing, a per se violation of the Sherman Antitrust Act: no proof of harm is needed, and a nod of agreement at a meeting can be evidence of a conspiracy. Each firm must set its own fee policy independently.

distractorExplanations.b: Disclosing the rate does not cure anything: the illegal act is the agreement between competitors, not a lack of transparency to sellers.
distractorExplanations.c: No state commission or trade association sets commission rates; fees are negotiated between broker and client, which is why agreeing on them is unlawful.
distractorExplanations.d: Leaving room for exceptions does not save it; an agreement among competitors on a standard rate is illegal even if individual deals deviate.

ct-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.prompt: A Connecticut deed describes a lot by metes and bounds from a point of beginning at an oak tree, 'thence east 300 feet to a stone wall.' The surveyor finds the stone wall is actually 312 feet east of the oak. Where does the boundary generally run?

options.a: At 300 feet, because stated distances control over physical monuments
options.b: At 306 feet, splitting the difference between the two measurements
options.c: At 300 feet, unless the deed's total acreage figure says otherwise
options.d: At the stone wall, because monuments control over stated distances

ct-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: When calls in a metes-and-bounds description conflict, courts apply a priority order: natural monuments, then artificial monuments, then courses (directions), then distances, with stated area last. The stone wall is a visible monument, so the line runs to the wall at 312 feet, and the description must still close back to the point of beginning.

distractorExplanations.a: This reverses the priority order: distances rank below monuments because a measuring error is more likely than a mistake about a visible wall.
distractorExplanations.b: Surveyors do not split the difference between conflicting calls; the higher-priority call, the monument, controls.
distractorExplanations.c: Stated acreage is the weakest call of all and gives way to monuments, courses and distances.

ct-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.prompt: A Connecticut town assesses a home at $245,000 and sets a mill rate of 28.5. The buyer's lender needs the annual property tax to set up the escrow account. What is the annual tax?

options.a: $698.25 a year

ct-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: A mill is one-tenth of a cent, so 1 mill means $1 of tax per $1,000 of assessed value. Tax = assessed value × mill rate ÷ 1,000 = $245,000 × 28.5 ÷ 1,000 = $6,982.50 per year. The mill rate is applied to the assessed value the town set, which already reflects any assessment ratio.

distractorExplanations.a: Divides by 10,000 instead of 1,000, so the result is ten times too small; 28.5 mills means $28.50 per $1,000 of assessed value.
distractorExplanations.b: Applies a 70% assessment ratio a second time; $245,000 is already the assessed value, so no further ratio is applied.
distractorExplanations.d: Treats the mill rate as a percentage (28.5 per 100); mills are per 1,000, so this overstates the tax tenfold.

de-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.prompt: A Delaware listing agent receives the buyer's $5,000 earnest-money check on a Friday. The seller asks the agent to 'just keep it in your desk drawer until the inspection clears next week.' Under the duty of accounting, what should the agent do?

options.a: Hold the check as asked, since the seller is the party who benefits from it
options.b: Deposit the check into the agent's own account and repay it at closing
options.c: Return the check to the buyer until the contingencies have been removed
options.d: Give the check promptly to the broker for deposit in the trust account

de-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: The duty of accounting requires a licensee to safeguard and account for every dollar received in a transaction. Earnest money belongs to neither the agent nor the seller yet, so it must go promptly to the broker for deposit in the escrow (trust) account within the time state rules set. A seller's convenience request does not override that duty.

distractorExplanations.a: The seller cannot waive trust-handling rules; an undeposited check sitting in a desk is unaccounted-for client money, exactly what the duty forbids.
distractorExplanations.b: Putting client money in a personal account is commingling (and possibly conversion), the most common trust-account violation.
distractorExplanations.c: Returning the deposit would undercut the contract; the buyer gave it as good-faith money to be held in escrow, not handed back on request.

de-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.prompt: A Delaware widower signs and notarizes a deed giving his house to his daughter, then locks it in his own safe, telling no one, planning to hand it over 'someday.' He dies before doing so. Does the daughter own the house under that deed?

options.a: No, because the deed was never delivered during the grantor's life
options.b: Yes, because a signed and notarized deed transfers title immediately
options.c: Yes, because the daughter can still accept the deed after his death
options.d: No, because a deed between family members must state a cash price

de-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: A deed transfers title only when it is delivered and accepted while the grantor is alive. Delivery means the grantor intends the deed to take effect now and gives up control over it. Keeping it in his own safe shows he kept control, so there was no delivery and the house passes through his estate. Notarization only makes a deed recordable.

distractorExplanations.b: Signing and acknowledgment make a deed eligible for recording, but title does not pass until the grantor delivers it with present intent.
distractorExplanations.c: Acceptance cannot cure a missing delivery; a deed cannot be delivered after the grantor's death, so the gift fails and the house goes through the estate.
distractorExplanations.d: Consideration is not required for a valid deed; a gift deed reciting love and affection is valid once it is delivered and accepted.

de-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.prompt: A Delaware investor sells a rental building at a $180,000 gain and completes a 1031 exchange into a like-kind replacement property, but takes $40,000 in cash out of the exchange. There is no mortgage on either property. How much gain is taxable this year?

options.a: $0 of the gain
options.b: $8,000 of the gain
options.c: $40,000 of the gain
options.d: $140,000 of the gain

de-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: A 1031 exchange defers gain only on value reinvested in like-kind property. Cash the investor keeps is 'boot' and is taxed in the year of the exchange, up to the total gain. Here the $40,000 of boot is recognized now; the remaining $180,000 − $40,000 = $140,000 of gain is deferred into the replacement property's basis.

distractorExplanations.a: A 1031 exchange is not a full shelter when cash comes out; boot received is taxable to the extent of the realized gain.
distractorExplanations.b: That is roughly the tax at a 20% rate on the boot; the question asks how much gain is recognized, which is the full $40,000.
distractorExplanations.d: That is the deferred portion ($180,000 − $40,000), which carries into the new property's basis instead of being taxed now.

enrolled-agent-readiness-check-practices.prompt: The IRS sends written notice of examination of Dana's 2024 return. Sixty days later her EA, Omar, files an amended return claiming a refund and wants to bill 20% of the refund. Under Circular 230, is that fee allowed?

options.a: No, Circular 230 bars contingent fees on any return or claim
options.b: Yes, the claim is filed within 120 days of the exam notice
options.c: Yes, provided the fee appears in a signed engagement letter
options.d: No, unless the fee is capped at 10% of the refund obtained

enrolled-agent-readiness-check-practices.explanation: Section 10.27 generally bars contingent fees but allows them for services tied to an IRS examination, including an amended return or refund claim filed within 120 days after the taxpayer receives written notice of the examination. Omar filed on day 60, inside that window.

distractorExplanations.a: Overstates the rule; Section 10.27 has exceptions for exam-related work, interest and penalty claims, and judicial proceedings.
distractorExplanations.c: A signed engagement letter does not create an exception; whether a contingent fee is allowed depends on the type of service.
distractorExplanations.d: Circular 230 sets no percentage cap; a contingent fee is either within an exception or barred, whatever its size.

enrolled-agent-readiness-check-individua.prompt: Jordan, a single filer, sells stock in 2025 for a $4,000 long-term capital gain and a $12,500 short-term capital loss, with no other capital transactions. How is the net loss treated?

options.a: $3,000 deduction; $9,500 short-term carryover
options.b: $3,000 deduction; $5,500 long-term carryover
options.c: $3,000 deduction; $5,500 short-term carryover
options.d: $8,500 deduction in 2025, with no carryover to 2026

enrolled-agent-readiness-check-individua.explanation: Net the gain against the loss: $12,500 − $4,000 = $8,500 net short-term loss. Individuals deduct up to $3,000 of net capital loss against ordinary income each year, so $8,500 − $3,000 = $5,500 carries forward and keeps its short-term character.

distractorExplanations.a: Skips netting the $4,000 long-term gain against the loss first; the carryover is $8,500 − $3,000, not $12,500 − $3,000.
distractorExplanations.b: Gets the amount right but the character wrong: the leftover loss came from short-term sales and carries over as short-term.
distractorExplanations.d: Ignores the $3,000 annual cap on deducting net capital losses against ordinary income for a single filer.

enrolled-agent-readiness-check-businesse.prompt: Maya, a sole proprietor with no wages or other business income, buys $80,000 of equipment and elects Section 179 for the full cost. Her business income before the deduction is $50,000. What is the result?

options.a: $80,000 deduction, creating a $30,000 net operating loss
options.b: $50,000 deduction, with the other $30,000 permanently lost
options.c: $80,000 deduction, since the cost is below the dollar limit
options.d: $50,000 deduction; $30,000 carries forward to future years

enrolled-agent-readiness-check-businesse.explanation: Section 179 is limited to taxable income from the taxpayer's active trades or businesses, including wages. Maya's limit is her $50,000 of business income, so she deducts $50,000; the disallowed $30,000 carries forward indefinitely, subject to the same limit in later years.

distractorExplanations.a: Section 179 cannot create or increase a loss because the business income limit caps it; bonus depreciation, by contrast, can create a loss.
distractorExplanations.b: The excess is not lost; Section 179 amounts disallowed by the income limit carry forward to later tax years.
distractorExplanations.c: Staying under the annual dollar limit is necessary but not enough; the separate business income limit still applies.

fl-real-estate-readiness-check-contracts.prompt: Carlos and his sister Dana took title to a Miami condo as joint tenants with right of survivorship, stated in the deed. Carlos dies, and his will leaves his real property to his son Mateo. Who owns the condo now?

options.a: Dana owns the entire condo by survivorship
options.b: Mateo and Dana, as tenants in common, half each
options.c: Mateo owns Carlos's half once the will is probated
options.d: Dana and Mateo hold it together as new joint tenants

fl-real-estate-readiness-check-contracts.explanation: Survivorship operates at the moment of death: Carlos's interest ends and Dana, the surviving joint tenant, holds the whole title. A joint tenant's share never enters the probate estate, so a will cannot pass it. In Florida the right of survivorship must be expressly stated in the deed, as it was here.

distractorExplanations.b: Describes the result of a tenancy in common; survivorship sends Carlos's share to Dana, not to his heir.
distractorExplanations.c: Assumes a will controls joint tenancy property; the share passed to Dana at death and never reached probate.
distractorExplanations.d: Joint tenancy needs the unities created together; an heir cannot step into one, and here Mateo takes nothing.

fl-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-a.prompt: An appraiser values a 10-year-old office building in Ocala. The site is worth $150,000, replacement cost new is $900,000, and the building has a 50-year economic life with straight-line depreciation. What value does the cost approach indicate?
fl-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-a.explanation: Cost approach = replacement cost new − accrued depreciation + site value. Depreciation is 10/50 = 20% of $900,000 = $180,000, leaving a depreciated building of $720,000. Adding the $150,000 site gives $870,000. Land does not wear out, so it is added after depreciation, not depreciated.

distractorExplanations.a: Stops at the depreciated building value ($720,000) and forgets to add the $150,000 site value back in.
distractorExplanations.b: Depreciates the land along with the building (80% of $1,050,000); land is not depreciated in the cost approach.
distractorExplanations.d: Adds site value to replacement cost new but skips the $180,000 of accrued depreciation on a 10-year-old building.

fl-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.prompt: Sarasota zoning allows backyard accessory dwellings, but a subdivision's recorded deed restrictions limit each lot to one single-family residence. A buyer plans to add a rental cottage after closing. Which rule controls what she can build?

options.a: Zoning, because public law overrides private covenants
options.b: Zoning, once the county issues a building permit
options.c: Whichever rule was adopted most recently
options.d: The deed restriction, as the stricter rule

fl-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Zoning and recorded deed restrictions both bind the lot, and the owner must satisfy each one. When they conflict, the more restrictive rule effectively controls: zoning permission does not cancel a private covenant, which other lot owners or the association can enforce by injunction. The buyer should read the restrictions before relying on zoning.

distractorExplanations.a: Confuses permission with override: zoning sets a public floor but does not erase stricter private covenants recorded on the lot.
distractorExplanations.b: A permit shows zoning compliance only; it does not release a recorded covenant, so neighbors or the HOA can still sue to enforce it.
distractorExplanations.c: Recency is not the test; both sets of rules bind the owner at once, and the more restrictive one sets the practical limit.

ga-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.prompt: Augusta owner Ted gives open listings to brokers Amy and Ben. Amy shows the house to buyer Kim and negotiates price and terms with Ted. Kim then calls Ben, who writes up an offer on those same terms, and Ted accepts. Who has earned the commission?

options.a: Amy, as the procuring cause of the sale
options.b: Ben, because he wrote the accepted offer
options.c: Amy and Ben, splitting one fee equally
options.d: Both, each owed a full fee by their listing

ga-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Under open listings the owner owes a commission only to the broker who is the procuring cause: the one whose efforts started an unbroken chain of events that produced the sale. Amy found Kim and negotiated the terms; Ben merely wrote up a deal Amy had already put together, so Amy earned the fee.

distractorExplanations.b: Writing the final offer is not enough; the commission follows the unbroken chain of effort that Amy started.
distractorExplanations.c: Open listings pay the procuring cause; they do not divide the fee among every broker who touched the deal.
distractorExplanations.d: Each open listing pays only if that broker is the procuring cause, so Ted owes one commission, to Amy, not two.

ga-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.prompt: For many years Glenn has farmed a strip of his neighbor's rural Georgia land under a signed permission letter the neighbor gave him. He now claims title to the strip by adverse possession. What is the main weakness in his claim?

options.a: He did not pay property taxes on the strip
options.b: His use was permissive, not hostile
options.c: Farming is not open and notorious use of land
options.d: He holds no recorded deed to the strip itself

ga-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Adverse possession requires possession that is actual, open and notorious, exclusive, continuous for the statutory period, and hostile, meaning without the owner's permission. The written permission letter makes Glenn a licensee, so no amount of farming time ripens into title until permission ends and truly hostile use begins.

distractorExplanations.a: Tax payment is an added element in some states, but it cannot cure this claim; use under permission is not hostile.
distractorExplanations.c: Visible farming is the kind of open, notorious use that puts an owner on notice; that element is satisfied here.
distractorExplanations.d: Color of title can shorten the required period, but a deed is not an element of adverse possession; the defect is permission.

ga-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.prompt: A Marietta home sells for $425,000 with a 6% total commission split 50/50 between the listing and selling brokerages. The selling agent, Tasha, is on a 70/30 split with her broker. How much does Tasha earn on the sale?
ga-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: Work the split from the top down. Total commission: $425,000 × 6% = $25,500. The selling brokerage receives half, $12,750. Tasha keeps 70% of her brokerage's share: $12,750 × 0.70 = $8,925. Her broker keeps the remaining 30%, $3,825.

distractorExplanations.a: That is the broker's 30% of the selling side; Tasha's 70% share is the larger portion, $8,925.
distractorExplanations.b: Splits the $12,750 selling side 50/50 again, applying the co-brokerage split twice instead of Tasha's 70%.
distractorExplanations.d: Takes 70% of the entire $25,500 commission, skipping the 50/50 split with the listing brokerage.

hi-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.prompt: A Hawaii listing agent copies '1,850 sq ft' from the seller's old appraisal into the MLS without checking. The buyer later measures 1,610 sq ft, and the county property record also shows 1,610. Which statement best describes the agent's exposure?

options.a: Liable for negligent misrepresentation for failing to use reasonable care
options.b: Not liable, because the figure came from the seller's own appraisal
options.c: Not liable, because buyers are expected to verify every MLS figure on their own
options.d: Liable for fraud, since a wrong number in a listing is presumed intentional

hi-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Agents owe reasonable care with material facts they can easily verify. The county record showed 1,610 sq ft, so repeating 1,850 unchecked is negligent misrepresentation, even with no intent to deceive.

distractorExplanations.b: Citing the seller's appraisal is no shield when a quick public-record check would have caught the error.
distractorExplanations.c: Buyer diligence does not erase the agent's own duty to avoid careless misstatements of material facts.
distractorExplanations.d: Fraud needs knowing or reckless falsity; this was carelessness, which is negligence.

hi-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.prompt: A Hawaii homeowner wants to add a garage, but her irregular, steep lot makes it impossible to meet the 20-foot front setback; the garage would sit 12 feet from the property line. Which zoning approval should she seek?

options.a: A special-use permit, since a garage is a use the zone does not list
options.b: A rezoning of her lot to a district with smaller setback requirements
options.c: A nonconforming-use certificate, since the lot predates the setback
options.d: A variance, since the lot's unusual shape creates a hardship

hi-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: A variance relaxes a dimensional rule such as a setback, height or lot-size limit when the property's unique physical conditions, here an irregular and steep lot, create a practical hardship the owner did not cause. A special-use (conditional-use) permit is for a use the zone allows only with approval, such as a church in a residential area; it does not waive setbacks.

distractorExplanations.a: A garage is a normal accessory use in a residential zone; the problem is the setback dimension, which a special-use permit does not waive.
distractorExplanations.b: Rezoning changes the rules for a whole area through a legislative act; rezoning one lot for one garage is disfavored and unnecessary.
distractorExplanations.c: Nonconforming status protects an existing use or structure that predates a rule; it does not authorize a new garage that violates it.

hi-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.prompt: A Hawaii investor buys a condo to rent out for $660,000, putting 20% down. The appraisal allocates $110,000 of the price to land. Using straight-line depreciation for residential rental property, what is the deduction for a full year?

options.b: $19,200 a year
options.c: $20,000 a year
options.d: $24,000 a year

hi-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: Residential rental property is depreciated straight-line over 27.5 years, and only the building is depreciable because land does not wear out. Basis = $660,000 − $110,000 land = $550,000. Annual deduction = $550,000 ÷ 27.5 = $20,000 for a full year. How the purchase was financed does not change the basis.

distractorExplanations.a: Uses 39 years, the recovery period for nonresidential (commercial) property; a rental condo is residential rental property at 27.5 years.
distractorExplanations.b: Depreciates the loan amount ($528,000 ÷ 27.5); basis comes from cost, not financing, so the down payment does not reduce it.
distractorExplanations.d: Includes the $110,000 of land ($660,000 ÷ 27.5); land is not depreciable, so it must be removed before dividing.

ia-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.prompt: Two Iowa brokers, upset that a new flat-fee brokerage is undercutting them, agree to tell their agents not to show any of the flat-fee firm's listings. One of their buyer's agents asks whether this is allowed. What is the best answer?

options.a: Allowed, because each broker may decide which listings its own agents will show
options.b: Allowed, as long as the two brokers do not also discuss commission rates
options.c: A breach of MLS etiquette, but not a matter for antitrust law
options.d: An illegal group boycott under antitrust law, even with no price talks

ia-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: When competitors agree to refuse to deal with another firm, that is a group boycott, a per se violation of the Sherman Antitrust Act. A single broker may make its own business decisions independently, but the agreement between two competing firms is what makes this illegal. Withholding listings also breaches duties owed to buyer clients.

distractorExplanations.a: Independent choices are lawful, but here two competing brokers agreed together to shut out a rival; the agreement itself is the violation.
distractorExplanations.b: Price-fixing and boycotts are separate antitrust violations; avoiding rate talk does not make a coordinated boycott legal.
distractorExplanations.c: Group boycotts violate federal antitrust law and can bring fines, damages and even criminal charges, not just MLS discipline.

ia-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.prompt: An Iowa farmer rents cropland from Ruth, who holds a life estate in it. He plants soybeans in May. Ruth dies in August, which ends the lease before harvest. Who has the right to the soybean crop?

options.a: The tenant, who may return to harvest the crop he planted
options.b: The remainderman, because growing crops pass with the land
options.c: Ruth's estate, because the crop grew while she held the land
options.d: The remainderman, who must repay the tenant for seed and labor

ia-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Emblements are annual crops produced by labor, such as soybeans or corn. When a tenancy of uncertain length ends through no fault of the tenant, as when the life tenant's death ends this lease, the tenant may re-enter and harvest the crop he planted. The crop is treated as his personal property, not as part of the land passing to the remainderman.

distractorExplanations.b: Growing crops normally pass with the land, but emblements are the exception for a tenant whose lease ended unexpectedly through no fault of his own.
distractorExplanations.c: Ruth's estate did not plant the crop; the doctrine protects the person whose labor produced it, which is the tenant.
distractorExplanations.d: The remainderman does not take the crop and reimburse costs; the tenant keeps the right to harvest the crop itself.

ia-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.prompt: An Iowa borrower's 5/1 ARM started at 7.00% with 2/2/5 caps (initial, periodic, lifetime). At the first adjustment, the index is 7.25% and the margin is 2.75%. What interest rate applies for year six?

options.a: 7.00% interest
options.b: 7.25% interest
options.c: 9.00% interest
options.d: 10.00% interest

ia-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: The fully indexed rate is index + margin = 7.25% + 2.75% = 10.00%. But the first adjustment is limited by the 2% initial cap: 7.00% + 2.00% = 9.00% maximum. The new rate is the lower of the two, 9.00%. The lifetime cap of 7.00% + 5.00% = 12.00% is not reached.

distractorExplanations.a: The rate is not frozen after the fixed period; at the first adjustment it resets toward index plus margin, limited by the caps.
distractorExplanations.b: Uses the index alone and forgets the lender's margin, which is added to the index at every adjustment.
distractorExplanations.d: This is the fully indexed rate, but the 2% initial adjustment cap limits the first increase to 9.00%.

id-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.prompt: An Idaho buyer's agent, Priya, learns the seller is paying her commission through the listing broker. The listing agent then asks her to 'help get your buyer up to full price, since we're the ones paying you.' Whom does Priya represent?

options.a: The seller, because the party who pays the commission is the client
options.b: Both parties equally, since the fee comes from the seller's proceeds
options.c: The listing broker, who controls the cooperative commission split
options.d: The buyer, because agency comes from the agreement, not who pays

id-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Agency is created by the agreement and the relationship of trust, not by the source of the money. Priya contracted to represent the buyer, so she owes the buyer loyalty, confidentiality and full disclosure even though the seller funds her fee. Pushing her buyer to full price at the listing side's request would breach those duties.

distractorExplanations.a: Compensation does not determine agency; a seller-paid fee to a buyer's agent is common and does not shift her loyalty to the seller.
distractorExplanations.b: Representing both sides would be dual agency, which requires informed written consent; the payment source does not create it.
distractorExplanations.c: The listing broker shares compensation through the cooperative arrangement but does not become Priya's client by doing so.

id-real-estate-readiness-check-id-licens.prompt: An Idaho licensee, Cole, wants to buy a fixer-upper listed by another brokerage as a personal investment. He plans to make the offer himself as a private buyer without mentioning that he is licensed. What should he do?

options.a: Make the offer as a private buyer, since he is not acting as an agent
options.b: Disclose his license status in writing in or with his offer
options.c: Have an unlicensed relative sign the offer so his license is not involved
options.d: Tell the listing agent verbally once the seller has accepted the offer

id-real-estate-readiness-check-id-licens.explanation: A licensee who buys or sells for his own account is still held to license-law standards. Licensing rules generally require written disclosure of licensed status to the other party, ideally in the offer itself, so the seller knows the buyer may have market expertise. Hiding the license as a 'private buyer' or through a straw buyer is misrepresentation.

distractorExplanations.a: Being a principal rather than an agent does not exempt him; license-law disclosure duties apply when licensees trade for themselves.
distractorExplanations.c: Using a straw buyer to hide his interest is misrepresentation and can bring discipline on top of the failure to disclose.
distractorExplanations.d: A verbal mention after acceptance is too late; the seller should learn of his license status in writing before agreeing to terms.

id-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.prompt: Two Idaho ranchers irrigate from the same creek. Hal's water right has a 1921 priority date; Vera's right, upstream of Hal, dates from 1978. In a drought year the creek cannot supply both. Whose right is satisfied first?

options.a: Hal's, because the earlier priority date is filled first
options.b: Vera's, because her land lies upstream and touches the creek first
options.c: Both cut back equally, as riparian owners sharing the creek
options.d: The rancher with more creek frontage, in proportion to that frontage

id-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Idaho, like most Western states, allocates water by prior appropriation: 'first in time, first in right.' A water right is tied to its priority date and beneficial use, not to owning land on the bank. In a shortage the senior 1921 right is filled first, and a junior user such as Vera may have to curtail even though she is upstream.

distractorExplanations.b: Location on the stream gives no priority under prior appropriation; an upstream junior user must curtail so water reaches a downstream senior right.
distractorExplanations.c: Equal sharing among bank owners reflects the riparian doctrine used mostly in Eastern states; Idaho applies prior appropriation instead.
distractorExplanations.d: Frontage matters under riparian thinking, not prior appropriation; the right depends on its priority date and beneficial use.

il-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.prompt: Naperville broker Ellen's listing with seller Raj expired last month unsold. During the listing, Raj confided that he would accept $18,000 below his asking price. Now Ellen represents a buyer who wants to offer on Raj's home and asks his bottom line. What should Ellen do?

options.a: Share it, since her duties to Raj ended with the listing
options.b: Keep it confidential; that duty survives the listing
options.c: Share it if Raj has since listed with another firm
options.d: Disclose it once the buyer signs a confidentiality pledge

il-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Most agency duties end when a listing expires, but the duty to protect a former client's confidential information continues afterward. Raj's willingness to accept less is exactly the kind of fact that would weaken his bargaining position, so Ellen may not reveal it, even though she now represents a buyer for that home.

distractorExplanations.a: Confuses ending the agency with ending every duty; confidentiality outlasts the listing and protects Raj's negotiating position.
distractorExplanations.c: Raj's choice of a new firm does not release Ellen; the information was given to her in confidence and stays protected.
distractorExplanations.d: A buyer's promise cannot authorize disclosure; the former client, Raj, is the person who could consent to releasing it.

il-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.prompt: Priya buys an Evanston house fronting Lake Michigan, while her cousin buys acreage along the Fox River. At closing, their attorney explains the water rights that come with each parcel. Which description is accurate?

options.a: Both hold riparian rights, since each borders water
options.b: Priya has riparian rights and her cousin has littoral rights
options.c: Priya's are littoral rights; the cousin's are riparian
options.d: Both hold littoral rights, since both waters are navigable

il-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Littoral rights belong to owners bordering large standing bodies of water such as lakes and oceans. Riparian rights belong to owners along flowing water such as rivers and streams, and include reasonable use of that water. Priya's Lake Michigan frontage carries littoral rights; the Fox River acreage carries riparian rights.

distractorExplanations.a: Riparian rights attach to flowing rivers and streams; land on a large lake such as Lake Michigan carries littoral rights.
distractorExplanations.b: Reverses the terms: littoral rights go with lakes and oceans, riparian rights with rivers like the Fox.
distractorExplanations.d: Navigability does not decide the label; a river is flowing water, so the Fox River parcel carries riparian rights.

il-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-m.prompt: Chicago buyers take a $240,000, 30-year fixed mortgage at 6% interest with a monthly principal-and-interest payment of $1,438.92. How much of the very first monthly payment reduces the loan balance?

options.a: $238.92 to principal
options.b: $666.67 to principal
options.c: $1,200.00 to principal
options.d: $1,438.92 to principal

il-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-m.explanation: First-month interest is the annual rate on the full balance for one month: $240,000 × 6% ÷ 12 = $1,200. The rest of the payment goes to principal: $1,438.92 − $1,200 = $238.92. The balance drops slightly each month, so later payments shift steadily toward principal.

distractorExplanations.b: Divides the loan by 360 payments as if principal were repaid in equal slices; amortized loans are front-loaded with interest.
distractorExplanations.c: That is the interest portion of the first payment, not the amount that reduces the principal balance.
distractorExplanations.d: That is the whole payment; $1,200 of it is interest, which does not reduce the loan balance.

in-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.prompt: An Indiana agent hands a seller an exclusive listing agreement stating that it 'remains in effect until the property is sold.' The seller asks whether an open-ended term like that is normal. What is the best response?

options.a: It is fine, because exclusive listings run until a buyer closes
options.b: It is fine if the seller may cancel with 30 days' written notice
options.c: It needs a specific end date, as license rules generally require
options.d: It is fine, because the agency relationship automatically ends at closing

in-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Real estate license laws generally require an exclusive listing to state a definite expiration date, and many bar automatic renewals. An open-ended term ties the seller to one broker indefinitely, so the broker should write in a specific date. The listing can still end earlier by sale, mutual agreement, or the death or incapacity of a party.

distractorExplanations.a: Exclusive listings are not open-ended by nature; they must state a fixed term so the seller is not bound to one broker indefinitely.
distractorExplanations.b: A cancellation clause does not cure the problem; license rules look for a definite expiration date written into the agreement.
distractorExplanations.d: Closing is one way a listing ends, but the agreement still needs a set end date in case the property never sells.

in-real-estate-readiness-check-in-licens.prompt: After closing, a grateful Indiana seller writes a $2,000 'thank-you' check payable directly to Jenna, the licensee who represented him, who works under managing broker Tom. What should Jenna do with the check?

options.a: Deposit it in her own account, since a gift is not a real estate commission
options.b: Keep it, as long as she reports it as income on her tax return
options.c: Split it with the buyer's agent to keep the cooperating fee fair
options.d: Give it to Tom, since compensation must come through her managing broker

in-real-estate-readiness-check-in-licens.explanation: A licensee may accept compensation for real estate activity only from the managing broker she works under. A 'thank-you' check tied to the transaction is compensation, not a personal gift, so Jenna should turn it over to Tom, who can pay her under their agreement. Taking it directly exposes her to license discipline.

distractorExplanations.a: Calling it a gift does not change its nature; money paid because of the transaction is compensation that must flow through the managing broker.
distractorExplanations.b: Tax reporting is a separate issue; license law still bars a licensee from accepting transaction compensation directly from a client.
distractorExplanations.c: Sharing it with another licensee compounds the problem; compensation is paid broker to broker, not from one agent to another.

in-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.prompt: Indiana's highway agency takes a 30-foot strip of Dale's commercial parcel for a road widening. Appraisals: $420,000 before the taking, $335,000 after; the strip alone is worth $40,000. Under the before-and-after method, what is just compensation?

options.a: $85,000 to Dale
options.b: $125,000 to Dale
options.c: $335,000 to Dale
options.d: $420,000 to Dale

in-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Under the before-and-after method, just compensation for a partial taking is the drop in the whole property's market value: $420,000 − $335,000 = $85,000. That figure already includes the $40,000 strip plus $45,000 of severance damage to the land Dale keeps, so nothing is added on top.

distractorExplanations.b: Adds the $40,000 strip on top of the value drop, but the before-and-after difference already includes the strip, so this double counts it.
distractorExplanations.c: That is the remainder's value after the taking, which Dale keeps; compensation is the loss in value, not what is left.
distractorExplanations.d: That would pay for the whole parcel, but the agency took just a strip and Dale keeps the rest of the land.

ks-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.prompt: A Kansas owner lives in one unit of her fourplex and rents the other three herself, with no agent. She posts an online ad: 'Unit for rent, no children.' Under the federal Fair Housing Act, what is the result?

options.a: The ad is lawful because an owner-occupied fourplex is fully exempt from the Act
options.b: The ad is lawful because familial status is not a protected class
options.c: The ad violates the Act even though her rental decisions may be exempt
options.d: The ad is lawful because she did not use a broker or an MLS listing

ks-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: The federal Fair Housing Act exempts an owner who lives in a building of four or fewer units from most of its rules, but that exemption does not cover discriminatory advertising. 'No children' discriminates on familial status, a protected class since 1988, so the ad itself is illegal even if her choice of tenants might be exempt. State or local law may be stricter.

distractorExplanations.a: The owner-occupied exemption is not total: the ban on discriminatory notices and ads applies to every owner, exempt or not.
distractorExplanations.b: Familial status (households with children under 18) has been a federally protected class since the 1988 amendments.
distractorExplanations.d: Not using a broker matters for the single-family-home exemption; it does not make a discriminatory ad lawful for anyone.

ks-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.prompt: A Kansas couple's farm is their homestead. A supplier wins a $90,000 judgment against them for an unpaid business debt, and they also owe their bank on the mortgage they used to buy the farm. Which statement about homestead protection is most accurate?

options.a: It blocks both creditors, since a family homestead is exempt from forced sale
options.b: It protects against the bank but not against the supplier's judgment
options.c: It ends once a creditor's judgment exceeds the farm's market value
options.d: It can shield the farm from the supplier but not from the mortgage bank

ks-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Homestead laws shield a principal residence from forced sale by general creditors, like a supplier with a business-debt judgment. They do not defeat debts secured by the home itself, such as the purchase-money mortgage or property taxes.

distractorExplanations.a: The exemption stops general creditors, not lenders whose loans are secured by the home.
distractorExplanations.b: This reverses the rule: the mortgage is a voluntary lien that survives; the unsecured supplier is blocked.
distractorExplanations.c: Judgment size does not matter; what matters is whether the debt is secured by the home.

ks-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.prompt: A Kansas borrower has a $250,000 payment-option loan at 5.4% interest. This month she makes the minimum payment of $950. How much negative amortization is added to her loan balance this month?

options.a: $175 added
options.b: $950 added
options.c: $1,125 added
options.d: $2,100 added

ks-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: Monthly interest = $250,000 × 5.4% ÷ 12 = $1,125. The $950 payment falls $1,125 − $950 = $175 short of the interest due, so that unpaid $175 is added to principal: negative amortization. The balance grows to $250,175, and next month's interest is charged on the larger balance.

distractorExplanations.b: That is the payment itself; only the part of the interest the payment fails to cover is added to the balance.
distractorExplanations.c: That is the full month's interest; the $950 payment covers most of it, so only the $175 shortfall is capitalized.
distractorExplanations.d: That is roughly a year of $175 shortfalls ($175 × 12); the question asks about this month's payment only.

ky-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.prompt: A Kentucky seller signs a valid contract to sell a lakefront lot to Marcus, then gets a higher offer and refuses to close. Marcus has his financing ready and wants that particular lot, not money. Which remedy best fits his goal?

options.a: Sue for specific performance to compel the seller to convey the lot
options.b: Accept liquidated damages, the remedy the law requires for land deals
options.c: Seek rescission, which forces the seller to complete the sale
options.d: Record a lis pendens, which by itself transfers title to Marcus

ky-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Because every parcel of land is legally unique, money damages often cannot replace it, so a buyer who is ready, willing and able to perform may sue for specific performance, a court order compelling the seller to convey. Marcus has financing ready and wants this lot: the classic case for the remedy. A higher offer is no excuse to breach.

distractorExplanations.b: Liquidated damages apply only if the contract includes such a clause, and they usually serve the seller; nothing forces a buyer to take money for land.
distractorExplanations.c: Rescission undoes the contract and returns both parties to where they started, the opposite of forcing the sale.
distractorExplanations.d: A lis pendens warns the public that litigation over title is pending; it conveys nothing without a court judgment.

ky-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.prompt: A Kentucky buyer is purchasing a foreclosed house from a bank. The bank's deed promises good title against defects that arose while the bank owned the property, but not against earlier ones. Which type of deed is the bank giving?

options.a: A general warranty deed, covering defects back through the chain of title
options.b: A quitclaim deed, conveying whatever interest the bank happens to hold
options.c: A bargain and sale deed, which carries no covenants of any kind
options.d: A special warranty deed, limited to defects from the bank's ownership

ky-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: A special warranty deed warrants title only against defects created during the grantor's own ownership. Banks, estates and other fiduciaries use it because they know nothing about earlier owners. A general warranty deed covers the whole chain of title and a quitclaim makes no warranties, so the buyer should rely on an owner's title policy for earlier defects.

distractorExplanations.a: A general warranty deed covers defects from any point in the chain of title, broader than the limited promise this bank is making.
distractorExplanations.b: A quitclaim deed makes no promise about title at all; this bank is giving a limited warranty, which a quitclaim does not include.
distractorExplanations.c: A bargain and sale deed implies the grantor holds title but gives no express warranties; this bank expressly warrants its own period.

ky-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.prompt: A Kentucky homeowner defaults owing $212,000 on her mortgage, and the lender adds $8,000 in foreclosure costs. The foreclosure sale brings $175,000. Assuming no anti-deficiency rule applies, how large a deficiency judgment can the lender seek?

options.a: $0 deficiency
options.b: $37,000 deficiency
options.c: $45,000 deficiency
options.d: $220,000 deficiency

ky-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: A deficiency judgment covers what the foreclosure sale fails to repay. Total owed = $212,000 loan balance + $8,000 costs = $220,000. Deficiency = $220,000 − $175,000 sale proceeds = $45,000. The lender can collect that amount from the borrower's other assets as a personal judgment.

distractorExplanations.a: Foreclosure ends the borrower's ownership but not the remaining debt; where deficiency judgments are allowed, the shortfall stays collectible.
distractorExplanations.b: Leaves out the $8,000 of foreclosure costs, which are added to the debt before the sale proceeds are subtracted.
distractorExplanations.d: That is the total debt before the sale; the $175,000 the property brought at auction must be credited first.

la-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.prompt: A Louisiana seller is listing a house built in 1962. He has never tested for lead paint, does not want to, and says 'there is nothing to disclose.' What does federal law require before a buyer is bound by a purchase agreement?

options.a: Testing the home for lead and removing any lead paint found before sale
options.b: No lead steps, because the seller has no reports or known lead hazards
options.c: A lead disclosure when the buyer is financing with an FHA or VA loan
options.d: The EPA pamphlet, a lead disclosure and a 10-day chance to inspect

la-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: For housing built before 1978, federal law requires the seller to give the buyer the EPA lead pamphlet, disclose any known lead-based paint and reports (or state that none are known), include the Lead Warning Statement in the contract and offer a 10-day opportunity to inspect, which the buyer may waive. Sellers need not test or remove lead; agents must ensure compliance.
