options.b: When they sign a written buyer representation agreement
options.c: Before they submit an offer on the house
options.d: At closing, along with the other required disclosures

tx-real-estate-readiness-check-license-l.explanation: TREC requires license holders to provide the Information About Brokerage Services notice at the first substantive communication with a party about specific real estate. A meeting where buyers discuss their budget and a particular house qualifies, so Maria must deliver it now, before they share more confidential details or choose a type of representation.

distractorExplanations.b: Confuses the IABS notice with the representation agreement; the notice explains the agency options before a buyer chooses one.
distractorExplanations.c: Too late: by offer time the buyers have already discussed specific property and finances, which triggered the notice.
distractorExplanations.d: Treats the IABS as a closing document; it is a first-contact disclosure meant to inform the buyer before any dealings.

tx-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.prompt: Luis leases retail space in Austin for his bakery and bolts commercial ovens and display cases to the floor. His lease ends next month, and the landlord says the equipment now belongs to the building. What is Luis's right?

options.a: The equipment became the landlord's once it was bolted down
options.b: He may remove it if the lease lists each item by name
options.c: He may remove it before the lease ends, repairing damage
options.d: He may remove it, but must pay the landlord its value

tx-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Equipment a tenant installs for a business is a trade fixture and stays the tenant's personal property even when bolted down. The tenant may remove it before the lease term ends but must repair damage caused by removal. Trade fixtures left behind after the tenancy ends may be treated as abandoned to the landlord.

distractorExplanations.a: Applies the ordinary fixture test (method of attachment) to a business tenant; trade fixtures stay the tenant's property despite bolting.
distractorExplanations.b: The trade fixture rule protects business tenants without an itemized clause; a lease may change it, but silence does not forfeit it.
distractorExplanations.d: Trade fixtures belong to the tenant, so removal requires no payment; the tenant owes repair of removal damage, not the item's value.

tx-real-estate-readiness-check-contracts.prompt: Listing agent Rob tells a buyer that a Houston home has 'the best backyard on the street' and that the roof is 'two years old.' The roof is actually 14 years old, and Rob knew it. How are the two statements treated?

options.a: Both are puffing, since the buyer could inspect the roof
options.b: Both are misrepresentation, since neither is in writing
options.c: The roof age is puffing; the backyard claim is misrepresentation
options.d: The backyard is puffing; the roof age is misrepresentation

tx-real-estate-readiness-check-contracts.explanation: Puffing is an exaggerated opinion a reasonable buyer would not rely on as fact, such as 'best backyard.' A false statement of a verifiable fact, like roof age, that the agent knew was untrue is intentional misrepresentation. It can support license discipline and buyer claims even though the buyer could have ordered an inspection.

distractorExplanations.a: A buyer's chance to inspect does not turn a knowing false statement of fact into puffing; roof age is a verifiable fact.
distractorExplanations.b: Oral statements can be misrepresentation, and the backyard opinion is puffing whether spoken or written.
distractorExplanations.c: Reverses the test: subjective opinion ('best backyard') is puffing, while a false, checkable fact (roof age) is misrepresentation.

va-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.prompt: Under a 6-month exclusive agency listing with broker Dana Price, Richmond seller Marcus Hill finds his own buyer, a coworker, with no help from any licensee and closes in month four. What commission does Dana's brokerage earn?

options.a: The full commission, since the listing was in effect at closing
options.b: Half the commission, as the owner and broker split credit for the sale
options.c: No commission, because the owner procured the buyer himself
options.d: The listing-side share, since no cooperating broker took part

va-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: An exclusive agency listing makes the broker the sole agent entitled to a fee if any licensee sells the home, but the owner keeps the right to sell it himself without owing a commission. Marcus found the buyer with no licensee involved, so no fee is due. Only an exclusive-right-to-sell listing pays the broker no matter who finds the buyer.

distractorExplanations.a: Confuses exclusive agency with an exclusive-right-to-sell listing, the type that pays the broker even when the owner finds the buyer.
distractorExplanations.b: There is no automatic split rule. An owner-procured sale under exclusive agency earns the broker nothing, not a shared fee.
distractorExplanations.d: The listing-side share is still a commission. Under exclusive agency, a sale the owner procures himself owes the broker no fee.

va-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.prompt: Grace deeds her lake cabin 'to my brother Paul for life, then to my niece Rosa.' Paul dies in 2026 and his will leaves everything he owns to his son. Grace and Rosa are both alive. Who owns the cabin now?

options.a: Paul's son, because Paul's will passes the cabin to him
options.b: Grace, because the cabin reverts to her as the grantor
options.c: Grace and Rosa together, as tenants in common in equal shares
options.d: Rosa, because she holds the remainder interest

va-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: A life estate ends when the measuring life ends, so Paul had nothing to leave by will. Because Grace named a third party to take afterward, Rosa holds a remainder and becomes the fee simple owner at Paul's death. A reversion back to the grantor arises only when the deed names no one to take after the life tenant.

distractorExplanations.a: A life estate measured by Paul's own life ends at his death; it cannot pass under his will or to his heirs.
distractorExplanations.b: Reversion applies when the grantor names no one to take after the life tenant. Grace named Rosa, so Rosa holds a remainder.
distractorExplanations.c: Nothing in the deed splits ownership. Grace kept no future interest once she named Rosa to take after Paul.

va-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.prompt: Seller Ava Brooks closes at $380,000. Her loan payoff is $214,650, the brokerage fee is 5.5% of the price, and her other closing costs are $3,850. The buyer's $10,000 earnest money is applied to the price. What are Ava's net proceeds?
va-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: Net proceeds = price minus everything the seller pays. Fee: $380,000 × 5.5% = $20,900. Deductions: $214,650 + $20,900 + $3,850 = $239,400. Net: $380,000 − $239,400 = $140,600. The earnest money is part of the $380,000 the buyer pays, so it is neither added nor subtracted again.

distractorExplanations.b: Adds the $10,000 earnest money on top of the price. The deposit is already part of the $380,000, so counting it again overstates the net.
distractorExplanations.c: Charges the 5.5% fee on Ava's equity ($165,350) instead of the $380,000 sale price; brokerage fees are a percentage of the price.
distractorExplanations.d: Forgets the $20,900 brokerage fee (5.5% of $380,000), the largest seller expense after the loan payoff.

wa-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.prompt: Buyer Leo offers $512,000 for Nina's Spokane house. Nina counters at $520,000. Leo rejects the counter, and a day later Nina writes back that she now accepts his original $512,000 offer. Is there a binding contract?

options.a: Yes, because Nina accepted Leo's offer before he withdrew it
options.b: No; her counter ended Leo's offer, so her reply is a new offer
options.c: Yes, because an offer stays open until its stated deadline passes
options.d: No, because acceptance must come from Nina's listing broker

wa-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: A counteroffer rejects and terminates the original offer; under the mirror-image rule, acceptance must match the offer exactly. Once Nina countered, Leo's $512,000 offer no longer existed for her to accept. Her later message is a new offer at $512,000, and no contract forms unless Leo accepts it.

distractorExplanations.a: Leo never needed to withdraw. Nina's own counteroffer had already terminated his offer, so nothing was left to accept.
distractorExplanations.c: A stated deadline keeps an offer open only until it is rejected; a counteroffer is a rejection that ends it early.
distractorExplanations.d: The seller, not her broker, is the party who accepts. The problem is that Leo's offer had already ended, not who signed.

wa-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.prompt: For 14 years, longer than the state's prescriptive period, Omar has openly driven across a corner of neighbor Beth's lot to reach his garage, never asking permission. His lot also fronts a public street. Beth now plans a fence. Omar's best claim is:

options.a: Title to the corner strip by adverse possession
options.b: An easement by necessity across Beth's lot
options.c: A revocable license that ended when Beth objected
options.d: An easement by prescription to keep crossing

wa-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Open, notorious, continuous, and hostile (unpermitted) use for the full statutory period creates an easement by prescription. Omar used the strip as a driveway, not as land he possessed exclusively, so he gains a right to use it rather than title. Beth cannot shut that right off with a fence.

distractorExplanations.a: Adverse possession transfers title and requires exclusive possession; Omar only crossed the strip and never possessed it as an owner would.
distractorExplanations.b: An easement by necessity requires a landlocked parcel. Omar's lot fronts a public street, so he has other access.
distractorExplanations.c: A license exists only when the owner gives permission. Omar never asked, which is exactly what made his use hostile.

wa-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-a.prompt: Appraiser Kim is valuing a Bellevue subject home with a three-car garage and no pool. Comparable 2 sold for $968,000 and has a pool (market value $22,000) but no garage (market value $45,000). What is Comparable 2's adjusted sale price?
wa-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-a.explanation: Adjust the comparable to look like the subject, not the subject to look like the comp. Comp 2 has a pool the subject lacks, so subtract $22,000; it lacks the garage the subject has, so add $45,000. $968,000 − $22,000 + $45,000 = $991,000.

distractorExplanations.a: Subtracts both features. The missing garage makes the comp inferior to the subject, so $45,000 must be added, not deducted.
distractorExplanations.b: Reverses both signs, as if the subject were adjusted toward the comp: +$22,000 for the pool and −$45,000 for the garage.
distractorExplanations.d: Adds both features. The comp's extra pool makes it superior to the subject, so $22,000 must come off its price.
